title: Capture File Properties Dialog: Support packet w/o timestamps (bugfix)
description:
With formats like BLF some packets do not have a timestamp as they are
only used to store meta data. This patch makes sure that such packets
are ignored for calculating Time and Timespan.

notes.body:
This fixes the bug that with BLF files the Capture File Properties Dialog does not show correct values or not values at all.

This affects at least master, 4.6, 4.4.
Are there better defines to use than `G_MINDOUBLE` and `G_MAXDOUBLE`?
I suspect G_MAXDOUBLE is not a "valid" time so can that be checked instead of adding boolean values?
I wasn't sure what ranges upcoming file formats might have. But I guess G_MAXDOUBLE and G_MINDOUBLE could be used to encode "not valid".
changed this file in version 2 of the diff
Done
Should we use `DBL_MIN` and `DBL_MAX` from C's <float.h> instead?
Trying `DBL_MIN` and `DBL_MAX`.

> With formats like BLF some packets do not have a timestamp as they are only used to store meta data.

...and, if they only store metadata, they aren't packets, they're records of some other sort.

This doesn't show the first or last packet timestamps on a capture that begins with BLF metadata, even though there *are* packets in the capture (the capture from #20691). It *could* show the first packet timestamp by finding the first packet time stamp in the loop rather than before the loop. If so, it should report them as the first and last *timestamped* packet times.

Also, given that not all timestamped records are packets, should it report the first and last *packet* time - i.e.,, only look at records with a record type of `REC_TYPE_PACKET`) - or should it report the first and last *record* time (look at all records with time stamps, *and* report them as first and last *record* time)?

Yes, meta data is not packets. I meant to write objects. :grinning: 

The trace from that ticket seems to work for me:

![image.png](/uploads/6ad4c4b81701e9823a2b270258b21901/image.png){width=632 height=368}

This is the current master.

I assume that all objects - even though meta data - is encoded as `REC_TYPE_PACKET`. Isn't the EXPORTED_PDU not a packet too?

> I assume that all objects - even though meta data - is encoded as `REC_TYPE_PACKET`.

Yes, but that doesn't mean that metadata objects *are* packets in the sense of "data transmitted over a communication medium". Instead, it's a hack done in order to allow metadata not supported by pcap or pcapng to be written out along with *real* packets.

> Isn't the EXPORTED_PDU not a packet too?

LINKTYPE_EXPORTED_PDU was created for use by packets not containing lower-level protocols and not assigned their own LINKTYPE_ value; however, it was also used for metadata BLF objects, which, as noted, I don't consider to be packets.

Understood but I am not sure, what you are proposing.

Do you want to define an alternative to `REC_TYPE_PACKET`?
